choices: On Thanksgiving day, we drove north to Lake Erie to visit my cousins.
On Thanksgiving Day, we drove north to lake Erie to visit my cousins.
On Thanksgiving day, we drove north to lake Erie to visit my cousins.
On Thanksgiving Day, we drove north to Lake Erie to visit my cousins.
correct_answer: On Thanksgiving Day, we drove north to Lake Erie to visit my cousins.
explanation: "Thanksgiving Day" is the full holiday name, so Day is capitalized, and "Lake Erie" is a proper place name, so Lake is capitalized. Distractors lowercase "day" (treating it as a common noun) and/or "lake" (treating the generic part of a place name as common).
cap_rule: Holiday names: the word Day is capitalized as part of the holiday name; generic word "lake" capitalized in a named body of water

choices: Our class finished reading Bridge to Terabithia last spring.
Our class finished reading Bridge To Terabithia last spring.
Our class finished reading Bridge to Terabithia last Spring.
Our class finished reading Bridge To Terabithia last Spring.
correct_answer: Our class finished reading Bridge to Terabithia last spring.
explanation: In a title, a short preposition such as "to" stays lowercase unless it is first or last, and seasons are common nouns. Distractors capitalize every word of the title ("To") and/or capitalize the season "Spring" as if it were a month or holiday.
cap_rule: Titles of works: short prepositions inside a title stay lowercase; seasons are not capitalized

choices: My family moved from the south to a small town west of Chicago.
My family moved from the South to a small town west of Chicago.
My family moved from the South to a small town West of Chicago.
My family moved from the south to a small town West of Chicago.
correct_answer: My family moved from the South to a small town west of Chicago.
explanation: "The South" names a region of the country and is capitalized; "west of Chicago" only gives a direction and is lowercase. Distractors lowercase the region and/or capitalize the direction.
cap_rule: Compass directions: a region (the South) is capitalized; a direction (west of) is not

choices: On Friday, Governor Ruiz met with the mayor of our town to discuss the new bridge.
On Friday, governor Ruiz met with the mayor of our town to discuss the new bridge.
On Friday, Governor Ruiz met with the Mayor of our town to discuss the new bridge.
On Friday, governor Ruiz met with the Mayor of our town to discuss the new bridge.
correct_answer: On Friday, Governor Ruiz met with the mayor of our town to discuss the new bridge.
explanation: A title is capitalized when it comes right before a name ("Governor Ruiz") but not when it is used as a common noun ("the mayor of our town"). Distractors lowercase the title before the name and/or capitalize the generic title.
cap_rule: Titles of office: capitalized directly before a name, lowercase when used generically after "the"

choices: Marisol has Chemistry during first period and Algebra II right after lunch.
Marisol has chemistry during first period and algebra II right after lunch.
Marisol has chemistry during first period and Algebra II right after lunch.
Marisol has Chemistry during first period and algebra II right after lunch.
correct_answer: Marisol has chemistry during first period and Algebra II right after lunch.
explanation: A general subject such as chemistry is a common noun, but a specific course title such as "Algebra II" is a proper noun. Distractors capitalize the general subject and/or lowercase the named course.
cap_rule: School subjects: general subject names are lowercase; specific numbered course titles are capitalized

choices: Grandpa called the Great Depression "A hard school" and said, "Nobody forgets being hungry."
Grandpa called the Great Depression "a hard school" and said, "nobody forgets being hungry."
Grandpa called the Great Depression "a hard school" and said, "Nobody forgets being hungry."
Grandpa called the Great Depression "A hard school" and said, "nobody forgets being hungry."
correct_answer: Grandpa called the Great Depression "a hard school" and said, "Nobody forgets being hungry."
explanation: The first quotation, "a hard school," is a fragment blended into the writer's sentence, so "a" stays lowercase; the second is a complete quoted sentence introduced with a comma, so "Nobody" is capitalized. Distractors capitalize the fragment (treating every quotation as a sentence) and/or lowercase the full sentence (treating it as a continuation after the comma).
cap_rule: Quotations: capitalize the first word of a quoted complete sentence, not of a quoted fragment worked into the sentence

prompt:
Which word correctly completes the sentence?

The magician made the coin ______ from his hand.
choices: dissappear
disappear
disapear
dissapear
explanation: dis + appear keeps one s and the double p of appear. Distractors double the s (dissappear), drop a p (disapear), or both (dissapear).
spelling_pattern: prefix dis- added to a base word: one s (dis + appear), double p kept from appear

choices: neccessary
necesary
neccesary
necessary
explanation: "Necessary" has one c and two s's. Distractors double the c, single the s, or swap which letter is doubled.

prompt:
Which word correctly completes the sentence?

I will ______ finish my project before the weekend.
choices: definately
definitly
definatly
definitely
explanation: definite + ly: the root "finite" has an i, and the e is kept before -ly. Distractors write a for i (definately), drop the e (definitly), or both (definatly).
spelling_pattern: root finite keeps i and silent e before -ly (definite + ly)

prompt:
Which word correctly completes the sentence?

Voting in the student election is a ______ that every member shares.
choices: priviledge
privilege
privelege
priveledge
explanation: "Privilege" has no d (unlike knowledge or ledge) and an i in the second syllable. Distractors add a d (priviledge), write e for the unstressed i (privelege), or both (priveledge).
spelling_pattern: no d before the final ge, and i (not e) in the second syllable (privilege)

prompt:
Which word correctly completes the sentence?

The drummer kept a steady ______ while the band tuned their guitars.
choices: rhythm
rythm
rhythem
rythem
explanation: "Rhythm" (from Greek rhythmos) has a silent h after the r and no written vowel in its second syllable. Distractors drop the h (rythm), insert an e for the sound heard before m (rhythem), or both (rythem).
spelling_pattern: silent h after r and no vowel letter before the final m (rhythm)

prompt:
Which word correctly completes the sentence?

Her careful notes proved ______ when the team rebuilt the experiment.
choices: indispensible
indespensable
indispensable
indespensible
explanation: in + dispense + able: the suffix is -able (dispensable), and the prefix syllable is "dis," not "des." Distractors use -ible (indispensible), write the unstressed vowel as e (indespensable), or both.
spelling_pattern: -able vs -ible suffix plus unstressed i in the prefix in- / dis- (indispensable)
